newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: FOCUS-BIRZHU REVISED FORECAST NOT SEEN HITTING PRICE.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-BIRZHU REVISED FORECAST NOT SEEN HITTING PRICE.

text.p: Birzhu Milk's announcement on Tuesday that it expected to fall short of its initial 1997 profit forecast after it released its H1 results was not seen hitting its share price hard, dealers and analysts said.

The company, one of three corporates on the Vilnius bourse's elite five-stock official list, said on Tuesday that its net profit for the first six months of 1997 reached 2 million litas compared to 1.5 million litas in the same period last year.

The company's director general, Vladas Songaila, also told Reuters that the firm would not make its original profit forecast of 13 million litas this year because of an unexpected government decision to raise milk prices from August 1.
He said that the forecast would be cut by around three million litas.
The market's response to the news has been surprisingly unbearish.
Vilniaus Bank broker Kestutis Kvainauskas said that immediate conclusions based on interum results were premature.
"The company has invested into new production lines and there is no doubt that its profit will grow in the second half of the year," Kvainauskas said.
He also said that he was not expecting big price changes for Birzhu's share price, which traded at 9.05 litas on Monday.
He added that Lithuania's underdevloped market still often failed to respond to corporate news and results.
Arvydas Jacikevichius of Suprema brokerage said he was expecting the price of Birzhu Milk to go down a bit but not much.
"Birzhu Milk is a growing firm and its investors are targeting long-term profits," Jacikevichius said.

"Earlier monthly results results were suggesting that the company's profit will not rise as quickly as the company planned, at least in the first half of the year," Richardas Sudeika, an analyst from Vilfima brokerage told Reuters.
"We stick to our forecast that Birzhu Milk's net profit for the whole year will not exceed six million litas," Sudeika added.
